pages.title: Addendum Studio

006  
Addendum Studio — Crew Payment Rules Engine
  Exit Page  

Addendum Studio


Designed and built an internal B2B tool for ReelShort productions that turns crew deal memos and timecards into signed Payment & Addendum Calculations — encoding state overtime law, compounding fee logic and approval controls, so a whole production's paperwork is produced as one batch instead of one document at a time.

ROLE

PRODUCT DESIGNER
DESIGN ENGINEERSCOPE

Research & Rules Modeling
UIUX Design
Front-end Build

｜27 contractors ｜7 departments ｜8 paperwork steps per person ｜~139 OT hours reconciled ｜21 addenda per production ｜3 location rule sets ｜7 fee categories ｜

  Overview& Context  

The addendum is one step in an eight-step pipeline — and the only one that involves maths.


Every contractor on a ReelShort shoot moves through the same paperwork pipeline, tracked row by row in a crew batch sheet. Seven of the steps are "send and collect". The addendum is different: it turns negotiated terms and the production's time record into a pay calculation the producer signs.

On the reference production — a 10-day Texas shoot with 12-hour contracted days — 27 contractors across 7 departments went through this pipeline, and 21 of them needed an addendum. Each one was rebuilt by hand in Word and a personal spreadsheet.

01Welcome letter
02Agreement
03W-9
04Invoice
05 · this projectAddendum
06Folder
07Payment
08Finance
Contractor paperwork pipeline, column by column in the crew batch sheet. When the addendum stalls, payment stalls.


   The Problem   

The hard part wasn't the document. It was everything feeding into it.


Each addendum looks like a one-page form. Underneath sit three messy inputs — a free-text deal memo, a timecard export and a location rule — that only someone who knew the rules could reconcile. I started from the real crew batch sheet and traced every number on a signed addendum back to its source.

Anatomy of the crew batch — department header rows, a free-text deal column, derived OT figures and status columns in one sheet. Names and amounts are fictional, calculated with the real rules.


Deals arrive as sentences
"$1000 flat prep, $350 / 12 hour shoot day, 10 days" had to be re-read and split into rate, hours, days and fees before any maths could start.Overtime law differs by state
California pays 1.5× after 8 hours and 2× after 12; Texas and most other locations stop at 1.5×.
Fees compound on each other
Hourly rate is backed out of a weighted day; OT and meal penalties depend on it; agency fees apply to flat + base + OT, never to per-diems.Batch work, one-off tools
Dozens of contractors paid in weekly waves — but addenda were built one at a time, with signatures pasted in after the fact.


From a sentence to structured fields


"$1000 flat prep/wrap, $420 / shoot day, 12 hour day, 10 day shoot"
→
Flat fee · Prep & wrap$1,000.00
Principal day rate$420.00
Contracted hours12 hrs/day
Working days10


A 14-hour day is three pay rates in California — and two in Texas.


Contracted hours are folded into weighted bands to back out a true hourly rate; every OT hour from the production record is then re-priced per working day.

California
1× · hrs 1–81.5× · 8–122× · 12+
Texas / Other
1× · hrs 1–81.5× · over 8
0h4h8h12h14h
12-hr day, Texas8 + 4 × 1.5 = 14 weighted hrs
Hourly rate$420 ÷ 14 = $30.00
Recorded OT (1.65 hrs/day)1.65 × 1.5 × $30 × 10
OT fee on the addendum= $742.50



   Design Principles   

Model the rules once. Let the interface stay simple.


Derive, never type
Hourly rate, OT, meal penalty, agency fee and total are outputs. Nobody hand-edits a number the engine owns.The batch is the unit
Accountants think in productions and pay waves, so the home view is a project with progress and exposure.Enforce, don't explain
Order, validation and approval locks live in the product, replacing tribal knowledge.

BEFORE
① Read the free-text deal memo
② Copy last project's Word template
③ Rebuild formulas in a spreadsheet
④ Look up the state's OT tier
⑤ Type figures, paste a signature, export
⑥ Repeat for ~21 contractorsAFTER · ADDENDUM STUDIO
① Pick the project — location rules apply
② Import the crew batch CSV
③ Fix only records flagged "Needs fix"
④ Finalize approval — record locks
⑤ Batch-export every addendum as PDF


   01 Rules Engine   

A rules engine, not a template.


Choosing a location sets the overtime bands for every record on the project; changing a day rate re-derives hourly rate, OT, meal penalty and agency fee instantly. Each fee category is an optional, collapsible section with a live subtotal — and blank categories disappear from the final document.






   02 Built for Batches   

The production, not the document, is the unit of work.


The workspace opens on crew count, finalized ratio, records needing attention and the running project total. The queue carries each contractor's amount and status, and filters straight to the records that block a pay wave. CSV import uses alias lists and fuzzy header matching, so the crew sheet production already keeps becomes the input.






   03 Guardrails   

Guardrails over manuals.


Crew editing stays locked until the project is defined. Validation runs on every keystroke and marks the exact field that's wrong. Export is blocked while any record fails. Once a producer finalizes, approver, date and signature lock — payment lines stay editable, but approval can't drift silently.




   04 WYSIWYG   

What you see is what gets signed.


The right-hand pane is the actual print layout, updating live. Reviewers never reconcile a form against a separate output — the document is the interface, and switching to a California unit re-renders every preview with its own overtime law.




   Impact   

From a per-document chore to a per-production workflow.


~85%*less time to prepare a production's addenda batch
0manual formulas left in the addendum step
4 → 1tools consolidated: deal memo, template, sheet, PDF/signing
100%of exported records pass validation
Fewer payment re-issues
Location-aware OT and a visible formula target the most common re-issue: the wrong tier copied from another project.Approval you can audit
Finalized records lock signature and date — a clear line between draft and approved before each pay wave.Onboarding in minutes
A new coordinator can produce a correct addendum without learning the rules first.

What's next


Ingest OT hours straight from the production timecard export · write addendum status back to the crew batch sheet · replace uploaded signature images with a producer e-signature and audit trail.

* Estimated from walkthroughs of the previous manual process. Reference counts come from one ReelShort crew batch; product screens use fictional demo data and no personal or payment data is shown.
